transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-10
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (CTO), Samir Patel (Head of Infra), Lena Ortiz (Security), Tom Brooks (PM)

Summary notes (auto): POC to validate private network deployment in a single locked region with strict egress. Focus on peering vs PrivateLink; benchmarks include 99th percentile latency < 250ms for short prompts, sustained throughput for 50k tokens/day workload, KV cache behavior with session affinity.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for hopping on. quick round — Maya from Redwood, Diego our Solutions Engineer. how are we all?
[00:06] Priya Nair: Good, thanks. busy week but glad we could align.
[00:10] Samir Patel: Morning — Samir here, I manage infra. We'll drive the networking bits today.
[00:15] Diego Ramos: Great, quick agenda — talk high level POC goals, network topology options (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), egress constraints and region-locking, then benchmarks and timeline. sound ok?
[00:23] Tom Brooks: Yep good. Also want to confirm success criteria up front so we don't iterate forever.
[00:27] Lena Ortiz: from security: we'll need audit logging, KMS integration, and proof of no egress outside region.
[00:33] Maya Chen: Perfect. Priya, could you start with the business/tech objective for the POC?
[00:38] Priya Nair: Sure. we're experimenting integrating Rouge — our clinical summarization service — with an LLM endpoint for on-call summarization. primary constraint: PHI must stay in eu-central region and never leave our VPC except to the inference endpoint in the same region. So residency + locked egress is a must.
[00:55] Maya Chen: Got it. scope: 4-6 week POC, validate latency targets for 256-512 token prompts and throughput for baseline of 20 req/s peak, average 5 req/s, rough tokens/day ~50k. Does that align with what you've seen?
[01:10] Samir Patel: Yes that's close. We might spike to 40 req/s during batch processing windows but most traffic is steady.
[01:16] Diego Ramos: okay that's helpful. On the networking side, two main deployment patterns we've done: VPC peering into Redwood-managed VPCs or AWS PrivateLink where we publish an interface endpoint into the customer's VPC. Both keep traffic on the cloud fabric, but there are tradeoffs.
[01:30] Diego Ramos: With VPC peering you get direct routing, fewer hops, and easier source IP preservation, but it requires route table changes and cross-account peering — sometimes slower to approve with infra teams. PrivateLink is controlled, and you avoid transitive routing issues, but you have to manage ENIs and there's NAT behavior for outbound.
[01:48] Samir Patel: For us, the big question is egress — our security posture forbids any outbound to public internet even to vendor IPs. PrivateLink sounds promising, but does Redwood still egress to other regions for model fallback?
[02:01] Maya Chen: Good callout. For the POC we can guarantee same-region placement for the model endpoints. Redwood's routing can be configured to avoid cross-region fallbacks; Diego can show how we pin model variants to region.
[02:12] Diego Ramos: yes, we can pin. default runtime may prefer fallbacks in overloaded scenarios, but for a private deployment or dedicated capacity we set the routing policy to strict-region-only. also we support an allowlist of egress IPs if you choose peering.
[02:27] Lena Ortiz: allowlist of IPs is fine only if they are within our region and static. we also need TLS termination and HSM/KMS integration — our keys must never leave our control.
[02:40] Maya Chen: we have KMS integrations and for Private deployments we support bring-your-own-KMS (BYOK) via customer-managed keys. Diego, can you highlight the audit logging?
[02:49] Diego Ramos: Sure. We produce request-level audit logs that can be forwarded to your S3/Bucket or CloudWatch in-region. For the POC we can enable detailed logs and redact sensitive fields by default. note: that adds overhead and slightly higher latency for large payloads.
[03:04] Tom Brooks: What about token-level cost vs latency tradeoff? if we enable detailed logs and async writes, will that push us over latency SLOs?
[03:12] Diego Ramos: Possibly — log writes happen asynchronously but some checks are sync. For the target p99 <250ms for short prompts, with logging enabled we expect p50 to remain low but p99 can increase by ~30-60ms depending on payload size. We can test with the bench harness.
[03:27] Priya Nair: okay we need to see actual numbers. what does Redwood need from us to run bench?
[03:32] Diego Ramos: sample traffic shape (QPS curve), representative prompt lengths and a set of prompts — ideally 100-200 prompts covering the common and edge cases. also network ACLs and whether you'll permit an interface endpoint or peering.
[03:44] Samir Patel: I'll compile QPS and examples. about region-lockdown: we run in eu-central and require no egress outside eu-central. can you confirm model placement there?
[03:53] Maya Chen: Redwood has model variants in eu-central; for POC we'll request Dedicated capacity in that region so models and KV caches stay in-region. Diego can pin the placement.
[04:00] Diego Ramos: Correct. We'll set placement constraints and routing policy that disallow cross-region fallback. If capacity is exceeded we can auto-scale within the dedicated pool or failover to a pre-approved smaller variant — but that would need signoff.
[04:12] Lena Ortiz: We need deterministic fail behaviors documented. automatic fallback to another region is a no-go.
[04:17] Maya Chen: Understood. We'll include explicit rollback/failover policies in the POC runbook.
[04:22] Tom Brooks: Benchmarks — what do you propose we measure in the 2-week benchmark phase?
[04:27] Diego Ramos: Proposed: p50 and p99 latency for three prompt buckets (short 64-256 tokens, medium 256-1024, long >1k), sustained throughput test at your peak QPS for 15 minutes, cache-hit rate with session affinity tests, cold-start behavior for new sessions, and end-to-end TLS overhead. Also measure CPU/GPU utilization on the dedicated nodes so you can model cost.
[04:50] Priya Nair: Good. success criteria from product perspective: p99 <250ms for short prompts, 99.9% success rate during sustained load, audit logs forwarded in-region, and no egress observed. cost target TBD but want to compare to in-house $/token estimate.
[05:06] Maya Chen: Noted. Diego, for the POC sizing, given 50k tokens/day and peaks up to 40 req/s, what capacity do you recommend?
[05:16] Diego Ramos: We'll size by concurrent tokens in flight. For interactive short prompts, concurrency drives throughput. rough starting point: a single nvidia-4 GPU class instance in dedicated pool should handle baseline interactive load, but for headroom and predictable p99 we recommend 2 nodes with autoscaling off initially — keeps behavior deterministic. We'll provide a recommended config in writing.
[05:35] Samir Patel: We prefer deterministic capacity during POC so we can attribute latency to processing not autoscale.
[05:40] Diego Ramos: Makes sense. We'll propose a reserved 2-node pool for the 6-week POC.
[05:45] Tom Brooks: What about PrivateLink's ENI limits? we have a VPC with limited IP space.
[05:52] Diego Ramos: PrivateLink does require ENIs in subnets and will consume IPs; with peering you avoid that but you need cross-account routes. If IP space is tight, peering might be preferable. We'll share a diagram + IP consumption examples.
[06:05] Priya Nair: For compliance we need the ability to audit exactly which model weights were used and model versioning to replay. is that possible?
[06:13] Maya Chen: yes, Redwood retains model version metadata per request and we can include model hash in the logs. Diego will show retention options.
[06:20] Lena Ortiz: Also want to validate encryption in transit and at rest. proofs?
[06:25] Diego Ramos: TLS for transit, and at rest we support your KMS. For POC we'll get you the encryption certificate chain and the KMS flow diagram.
[06:33] Maya Chen: Quick timeline proposal: Week 0 - sign SOW and exchange network configs; Week 1 - network setup and basic connectivity test; Week 2 - deploy dedicated capacity and run initial smoke; Week 3 - benchmark window; Week 4-5 - iterate on tuning; Week 6 - run final acceptance and wrap. Is 6 weeks still acceptable?
[06:55] Priya Nair: Yes, that works for our Q1 pilot gating.
[06:59] Tom Brooks: Who will be our primary contact for network changes?
[07:03] Samir Patel: that's me. I'll coordinate with our cloud team and security.
[07:07] Maya Chen: Great. For the bench harness, we can use a simple loader (we have a k6-based harness) that you can run from an EC2 in-region to simulate the QPS with the correct source IPs. We'll attach the harness and a sample script.
[07:21] Samir Patel: nice. on the data side, PHI redaction — do you recommend client-side redaction or server-side?
[07:28] Diego Ramos: client-side redaction is safest since the data never reaches the model. but we also offer automatic redaction post-request and we can redact before logs persist. If you can do minimal client-side redaction during POC, that reduces risk and lets us measure end-to-end latency.
[07:44] Lena Ortiz: we'll likely do a hybrid approach — redact top-level PHI client-side, and redact finer-grained fields in transit. need to see how Redwood tags fields.
[07:52] Diego Ramos: we can provide a redaction spec and example filters.
[07:56] Maya Chen: any blocker on compliance paperwork? we can share our SOC2 plus an addendum for the POC.
[08:03] Lena Ortiz: we'll need SOC2 and ISO cert copies, and a data processing addendum. our legal will review.
[08:09] Maya Chen: noted. we'll upload those to the shared drive.
[08:12] Tom Brooks: on cost modeling — how will we present cost during POC vs projected prod?
[08:18] Maya Chen: we'll provide a cost model: tokens/day * unit cost + reserved node cost. Diego will include GPU-hour estimations. Also show how batching and KV cache impacts unit economics.
[08:29] Diego Ramos: for example with a 2-node pool and your traffic shape, estimated monthly cost extrapolated from POC is in the deck we'll share. but POC will focus on comparatives.
[08:37] Priya Nair: ok. circling back: egress detection — how will we validate that nothing left the region?
[08:44] Diego Ramos: two parts: network side we can provide VPC flow logs and we will publish egress IPs for any vendor-managed NAT so you can cross-check. application side we include request logs with destination metadata. We'll run a packet-capture smoke if you want during the bench.
[08:59] Samir Patel: packet-capture would be helpful. we'll run it on the EC2 client sim.
[09:03] Maya Chen: good. any other concerns?
[09:06] Priya Nair: timeline for getting the SOC2 and KMS docs — do you have those ready?
[09:11] Maya Chen: yes we have SOC2 and KMS integration docs; I'll share with you after the call.
[09:15] Lena Ortiz: and do you have a standard SRA or risk acceptance template?
[09:19] Maya Chen: yes, Redwood has an SRA template and we can pre-fill parts for the POC.
[09:23] Tom Brooks: one operational question: can logs be forwarded to our SIEM in-region?
[09:27] Diego Ramos: yes, we can forward logs to your CloudWatch/Splunk endpoint or S3 bucket. we'll configure retention per your policy.
[09:33] Priya Nair: Excellent. anything on the model side? versioning, quantization?
[09:38] Diego Ramos: for POC we'll use the verified open model variant in eu-central. quantization is optional; we don't recommend aggressive quantization for clinical use during POC until you validate output fidelity.
[09:50] Maya Chen: ok. let's summarize next steps and owners.
[09:53] Maya Chen: Action: Maya to send SOC2 pack, pricing and SOW draft.
[09:58] Diego Ramos: Action: Diego to share PrivateLink vs Peering diagram, bench harness, and recommended dedicated pool sizes.
[10:04] Samir Patel: Action: Samir to send traffic profile, allowed IPs, and confirm ENI/IP space constraints.
[10:11] Lena Ortiz: Action: Lena to review SOC2 and confirm KMS requirements.
[10:16] Priya Nair: We'll aim to sign SOW by next Tuesday so you can start week 0 activities.
[10:21] Maya Chen: that sounds good. we'll slot bench window in week 3.
[10:24] Tom Brooks: Any follow-ups on failure modes? we want the runbook for deterministic failure behaviors.
[10:30] Diego Ramos: we'll draft a POC runbook with failover behavior and rollback steps.
[10:33] Maya Chen: Great. Thanks all. we'll send the materials and schedule the network prep call.
[10:38] Priya Nair: Thanks — appreciate the clarity.
[10:41] Samir Patel: thanks everyone, talk soon.
[10:44] Lena Ortiz: bye.
